_comment: Advisories that have been assessed and do not apply to Sensei.
This file exists so `npm audit` can stay a hard CI gate. The alternative —
lowering the threshold or appending `|| true` — turns the gate off for every
future advisory too, which is how a real one gets missed.
Every entry needs a reason and a review_by date. Once that date passes the
gate fails again, so an exception cannot quietly become permanent.
Adding an entry here is a security decision. It belongs in a PR that says so.

allow.title: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response
allow.reason: Only reachable through React Router's RSC mode and server actions. Sensei's web UI is a client-only SPA: HashRouter, three routes, no loaders, no actions, no server rendering, no RSC. There is no server-side route handler for the bypass to reach. Downgrading is not an option — every release below 7.12.0 carries 14 advisories including an unauthenticated RCE (GHSA-49rj-9fvp-4h2h), so 7.18.1 is strictly the safer choice until a patched 7.12+ ships.
